description:
Gurdwara Chhevin Patshahi stands in the small village of Chitti Gatti, in a garden by the roadside about eight kilometres from Mansehra in the Hazara hills of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Its name — Chhevin Patshahi, the "Sixth Sovereignty" — commemorates Guru Hargobind, the sixth Guru of the Sikhs (Guru from 1606 to 1644), who by tradition is said to have visited the site during his travels through the region. The gurdwara is a handsomely built, domed structure, and it is remembered above all for an unusual arrangement of shared sacred use: a stone Shiv Ling was worshipped on the upper floor of the building while the prakash of the Guru Granth Sahib was installed on the floor below, with Hindu priests officiating — an arrangement that reflects the closely intertwined Hindu and Sikh devotion of the frontier, where the Guru was honoured by Hindus and Sikhs alike. A fair was traditionally held here at Vaisakhi, enthusiastically attended by the communities of the surrounding hills. The building stands beside the Shiv Mandir of Chitti Gatti (recorded separately in this dataset), the two shrines together forming a single sacred spot. Following the Partition of 1947 the Sikh and Hindu populations of the area departed and regular worship ceased, though the structure survives as a monument to the region's plural religious past.

This account rests on Iqbal Qaiser's 1998 survey, which describes the gurdwara as “beautifully constructed,” with a stone Shiv Ling still in place on the upper floor where it once shared devotion with the Guru Granth Sahib below; the site is also entered in the Department of Archaeology's 1962 register of Sikh shrines in West Pakistan as a “Gurdwara Chitti Chatti” in Hazara district near Mansehra, illustrated there by a photograph captioned “Gurdwara at Mansehra.”

## Bibliography
- Iqbal Qaiser, *Historical Sikh Shrines in Pakistan* (Punjabi History Board, 1998), p. 228.
- Khan Mohammad Waliullah Khan, *Sikh Shrines in West Pakistan*, Memoir of the Department of Archaeology in Pakistan No. 3 (Department of Archaeology, Government of Pakistan, 1962), Appendix 2, "List of the Shrines."

coordinates are adjacent to the Shiv Mandir Chiti Ghati (row 69) and are approximate; the two sites are co-located at Chitti Gatti. Distinct from the Gurdwara Chhevin Patshahi at Hadiara in Lahore district.

This addition rests primarily on a single independently-verified source (Iqbal Qaiser, 1998) for its descriptive detail; the only other citable source found, the 1962 Department of Archaeology register, merely lists and locates the site without independently corroborating the description, so this has not yet been corroborated by a second full account. Note also: press coverage of a 2021 restoration of “a Sikh gurdwara in Mansehra district” (Tribune India, 10 July 2021) concerns a different, unrelated site — Sri Guru Singh Sabha, founded in 1905 — and must not be confused with this Guru-Hargobind-era shrine at Chitti Gatti.
